study_identification.title: Lifespan Normative Models of White Matter Fractional Anisotropy: Applications to Early Psychosis

clarity_of_research_objectives.reason: The introduction clearly outlines four specific aims for the study, covering model development, application to psychosis, multi-modal data fusion, and public release of the models.
clarity_of_research_objectives.supporting_text: The aims of this study are to: (i) develop normative models of Fractional Anisotropy (FA), the most widely used diffusion metric in neuroimaging [17], across major white matter tracts using a large dataset of over 25,000 healthy individuals across a broad age range... (ii) investigate white matter FA in early psychosis... (iii) we aim to illustrate the value of normative models for multi-modal data fusion... Finally, (iv) we release all models freely to the community via our existing open-source software platforms [19].

clear_definition_of_target_population.reason: The study clearly defines the clinical target population as 'early psychosis' and specifies that diagnosis was confirmed using the SCID-5. It also describes the healthy control population used for building the normative models, detailing the datasets and their age ranges.
clear_definition_of_target_population.supporting_text: Participants with early psychosis were diagnosed using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 (SCID-5) (First et al., 2015)... The construction of the lifespan dataset involved integrating data from five cohorts having high-quality multi-shell diffusion data, i.e.: the HCP Baby [20], HCP Development [21], HCP Young Adult [22], HCP Aging [23] datasets, and the UK Biobank [24].

clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_crite.reason: The paper mentions the datasets used for the normative model but does not detail the specific inclusion or exclusion criteria for these large-scale datasets, referring instead to the original publications. For the clinical application, it specifies the diagnostic criteria but lacks other details. It does, however, describe a data-driven exclusion criterion based on outlier detection.
clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_crite.supporting_text: In line with our prior work [46] we refit the models after excluding gross outliers having deviations larger than 5 standard deviations from the mean (Figure 1C).

validity_of_normative_modeling_outcome_m.reason: The primary outcome measure, Fractional Anisotropy (FA), is clearly defined as the metric of interest. The method for quantifying individual deviations (z-scores) from the normative model is also explicitly described.
validity_of_normative_modeling_outcome_m.supporting_text: The aims of this study are to: (i) develop normative models of Fractional Anisotropy (FA)... we applied these reference models to the HCP early psychosis (HCP-EP) dataset (N=173 with diffusion data -see supplementary table 2 for demographic information) in order to derive z-scores for each individual and tract.

handling_of_confounding_variables.reason: The paper explicitly states that the normative model incorporated age, sex, site, and self-reported race as covariates to account for their potential confounding effects.
handling_of_confounding_variables.supporting_text: A normative model was then fit to the training set for each white matter tract. The model incorporated several covariates, including sex, age, and dummy coded race, and site.

clarity_of_data_sources.reason: The paper clearly lists the specific datasets used to construct the normative model: HCP Baby, HCP Development, HCP Young Adult, HCP Aging, and the UK Biobank. For the clinical application, it specifies the HCP Early Psychosis (HCP-EP) dataset.
clarity_of_data_sources.supporting_text: The construction of the lifespan dataset involved integrating data from five cohorts having high-quality multi-shell diffusion data, i.e.: the HCP Baby [20], HCP Development [21], HCP Young Adult [22], HCP Aging [23] datasets, and the UK Biobank [24]... Next, we applied the model to the Human Connectome Project Early Psychosis (HCP-EP) dataset [18] (Jacobs et al., 2024)...

description_of_image_acquisition_protoco.reason: The paper states that the datasets used 'harmonized FSL-based pipelines' and had 'closely matched acquisition...pipelines'. It mentions 'multi-shell diffusion data' but does not provide specific acquisition parameters (e.g., TR, TE, resolution) in the main text or supplementary materials, instead referring to the original dataset documentation.
description_of_image_acquisition_protoco.supporting_text: The construction of the lifespan dataset involved integrating data from five cohorts having high-quality multi-shell diffusion data... The processing of these datasets followed harmonized FSL-based pipelines... These corrections were executed using the HCP-pipeline [42] for the HCP datasets while the UKB dataset was already processed according to the UKB documentation [43].

details_of_data_preprocessing.reason: The paper provides a clear description of the preprocessing pipeline in the Methods section and Figure 1A. It specifies the software (FSL-based pipelines, DTIfit, TBSS) and the key steps performed, such as intensity normalization, distortion/movement correction, DTI model estimation, and registration to a standard space.
details_of_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: The processing of these datasets followed harmonized FSL-based pipelines, summarized in Figure 1A. Initially, pre-processing was performed: B0 intensity normalization, correction for EPI distortions, eddy-current-induced and movement corrections... Subsequently, we estimated the DTI model using DTIfit... Following this, we ran Tract-Based Spatial Statistics (TBSS) [44] on the FA images...

clarity_of_data_partitioning_methods.reason: The paper explicitly states that the normative dataset was split into a 50% training set and a 50% test set. It also specifies that this split was stratified to ensure an even distribution of sex, race, dataset, and site. For the msCCA analysis, a 70/30 split is mentioned.
clarity_of_data_partitioning_methods.supporting_text: To prepare for the modelling stage, we began by splitting the dataset of subjects (N=24,915) into two equal groups: a test set (N=12,457) and a training set (N=12,457), stratified to ensure an even distribution of sex, race, dataset and site.

details_of_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The study clearly describes the statistical approach used. It specifies a 'warped Bayesian linear regression (BLR)' model, the use of a 'third-order polynomial B-spline basis expansion over age, with five evenly spaced knots', and a 'SinhArcsinh warping function'. It also mentions the use of the PCNtoolkit.
details_of_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: To address potential nonlinear effects and non-Gaussian distributions, we employed a warped Bayesian linear regression (BLR) model and used in previous research [4], [25]. This approach involved applying a third-order polynomial B-spline basis expansion over age, with five evenly spaced knots, combined with a SinhArcsinh warping function.

details_of_training_algorithm.reason: The paper specifies the model type (warped BLR) and its key components (B-splines, warping function) but does not provide details on the specific optimization algorithm used to train the model (e.g., variational inference, MCMC) or the criteria for convergence.
details_of_training_algorithm.supporting_text: we employed a warped Bayesian linear regression (BLR) model... This approach involved applying a third-order polynomial B-spline basis expansion over age, with five evenly spaced knots, combined with a SinhArcsinh warping function.

model_performance_evaluation_metrics.reason: The paper clearly states the three out-of-sample metrics used to assess the quality of the normative models: explained variance (EV), skewness, and kurtosis.
model_performance_evaluation_metrics.supporting_text: We assessed the quality of the normative modeling fit using three key out-ofsample metrics, namely explained variance (EV), evaluating the fit of the median regression line, in addition to skewness and kurtosis, which evaluate the shape of the distribution used to model the centiles.

implementation_of_internal_validation.reason: The study implemented internal validation by splitting the data into training and test sets. The model performance was evaluated on the held-out test set (out-of-sample), which is a standard and appropriate method for internal validation.
implementation_of_internal_validation.supporting_text: we began by splitting the dataset of subjects (N=24,915) into two equal groups: a test set (N=12,457) and a training set (N=12,457)... We assessed the quality of the normative modeling fit using three key out-ofsample metrics...

external_data_validation.reason: The study does not perform external validation in the sense of testing the trained model on a completely new, independent dataset from a different source. The application to the HCP-EP dataset is presented as a clinical use case and involves transfer learning to adapt the model, not as a validation of the original model's generalizability.
external_data_validation.supporting_text: Next, we applied the model to the Human Connectome Project Early Psychosis (HCP-EP) dataset... Using transfer learning, as in our previous work, we can efficiently adapt the models with only a small amount of calibration data to account for site-specific effect.

description_of_dataset_characteristics.reason: The paper provides demographic characteristics for both the normative and clinical datasets. Table S1 details the age, sex, and race distribution for the five normative cohorts. Table S2 provides N, age, sex, race, and clinical scores (PANSS) for the patient and control groups in the HCP-EP dataset.
description_of_dataset_characteristics.supporting_text: The demographic information is available in supplementary table 1... The dataset's demographic distribution comprises 37% females and 63% males, with a racial composition of 58% White, 28% Black, 9% Asian, 1% Mixed, and 3% Other.

performance_metrics_and_statistical_unce.reason: The paper reports point estimates for the model performance metrics (mean and standard deviation of EV, skewness, and kurtosis across all 48 tract models). However, it does not provide measures of statistical uncertainty for these metrics, such as confidence intervals for each model.
performance_metrics_and_statistical_unce.supporting_text: The mean (standard deviation) EV was 0.37 (0.10), indicating good fit across different models. Skewness, and kurtosis were respectively -0.09 ( 0.12) and 0.42 (0.27), which together indicate that the shape was also appropriate for the data.

consideration_for_reproducibility.reason: The study provides strong support for reproducibility. It explicitly states that all models are publicly available and provides a GitHub link for the code used to process data and train the models. It also mentions the software toolkits used.
consideration_for_reproducibility.supporting_text: All models are publicly available for community use... we provide these models to the field via our established no-code software platform [19] and via open-source software tools (https://github.com/ramonacirstian/fa_normative_modeling), so that others in the field can easily apply these models to their own data.

interpretation_specific_to_normative_mod.reason: The discussion section provides a thorough interpretation of the results from a normative modeling perspective. It emphasizes that the approach reveals a high degree of inter-individual heterogeneity in psychosis that is missed by traditional case-control analyses and discusses the clinical implications of identifying individual-level deviations.
interpretation_specific_to_normative_mod.supporting_text: We show a high degree of inter-individual heterogeneity in these individuals, evidenced by relative increases in both positive- and negative deviations from the normative model in individuals with psychosis relative to controls. These differences were evident despite an absence of case control effects, indicating that the differences were highly individualized.

additional_comments.additional_comments: This study provides a comprehensive and large-scale set of normative models for FA, which is a significant contribution to the field. A major strength is the public release of the models and code, greatly enhancing reproducibility. The application to early psychosis effectively demonstrates the utility of the normative approach in uncovering heterogeneity that is invisible to standard case-control methods. The multi-modal analysis linking brain deviations to symptoms is also a notable strength.
